neighbours.label: the token joining a body/mind-type substance pair (soul and body, mind and matter, flesh and blood)
fire: Plato taught that the soul and the body are separate, and that only the soul survives death.
For Descartes, mind and body are two utterly different kinds of substance.
Some philosophers hold that spirit and matter are two aspects of one reality.
Science fiction often asks whether a robot could ever be made of flesh and blood.
In this tradition, body and soul are united in a single living person.
The medieval theologians debated how the soul and the flesh relate to each other.
The old question of whether mind and brain are identical is still unresolved.
Aristotle described the soul and the body as the form and matter of one creature.
quiet: Plato taught that the soul is immortal, and that it lives on after a person dies.
For Descartes, thinking is the one activity that cannot be doubted.
Some philosophers hold that all of reality is ultimately made of atoms.
Science fiction often asks whether a robot could ever feel real pain.
In this tradition, a living person is seen as a single unified creature.
The medieval theologians debated how angels could move from place to place.
The old question of whether animals are conscious is still unresolved.
Aristotle described the parts of animals in careful and patient detail.
